script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - DAY

A cluttered room filled with posters, books, and various knick-knacks adorn the walls and shelves. A 20-something-year-old GAVIN sits on the couch, scrolling through his phone.

GAVIN (V.O)
(sighs) Another day, another rejection. I'm just not cut out for this world.

The door bursts open, and his BEST FRIEND, RACHEL, enters, holding a large pizza box.

RACHEL
Hey, mopey! I heard about the latest rejection.

Gavin looks up, surprised but relieved.

GAVIN
How'd you-?

RACHEL
You know me, Mr. Facebook stalker. You didn't hide it that well.

Gavin chuckles and shakes his head.

GAVIN
Well, this one really stung. I mean, I thought my script had a shot this time.

Rachel sets the pizza on the coffee table and sits down next to him.

RACHEL
I'm sure it did, Gav. But you know what they say: keep writing, keep improving.

Gavin nods, a determined look in his eyes.

GAVIN
You're right. I'll keep at it.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Gavin and Rachel sit in a quiet corner, laptops open in front of them. Gavin types away at his script while Rachel gives him occasional suggestions and encouragement.

INT. APARTMENT KITCHEN - NIGHT

Gavin cooks dinner for Rachel, who sits at the table, reading a book. They share stories and laughs as they eat.

GAVIN
(smiling)
You know, Rachel, sometimes I feel like I don't know who I am without my writing.

RACHEL
(looking up from her book)
But you are more than just a writer, Gav. You're a friend, a son, a brother, a partner. And those things don't depend on your success or failure in the writing world.

Gavin nods, considering her words.

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - DAY

Gavin sits on the couch, surrounded by stacks of rejection letters. Rachel enters, holding a framed photograph.

RACHEL
I was going through some old things and found this. I thought it might cheer you up.

She hands him the photo of him as a child, holding a pencil and a stack of paper.

GAVIN
(smiling)
I think it already has. Thanks, Rachel.

INT. LOCAL THEATER - NIGHT

Gavin sits in the dark theater, watching the opening credits of his first produced play. He looks over at Rachel, who sits next to him, beaming with pride.

GAVIN
(whispering)
We did it.

RACHEL
(smiling)
We sure did.

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - DAY

Gavin sits on the couch, holding the first copy of his published book in his hands. Rachel enters, holding a large bouquet of flowers.

RACHEL
Congratulations, Mr. Published Author!

Gavin beams with pride as they celebrate his achievement together.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
